chapter: Early recordings and arrival in New York
title: Saturday Swing Club, the New Yorker piece and Joe Helbock
summary: Les Lieber's Columbia show and the New Yorker article, after which Joe Helbock of the Onyx Club changed his attitude.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: You know, just about that time, the Columbia put the Saturday Swing Club on the stage at Loew's State live, along with some other acts -- Les Lieber who plays a (inaudible) was playing a penny whistle.
Right now, he heads an organization called
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

You know, Les Lieber. So Les Lieber was on that bill. And he was playing his penny whistle there. And some other acts which I don't quite remember, but Leith Stevens was the band and Paul Douglas was the announcer. In fact, on the air when the program came on, Paul Douglas would say, "The Saturday Night Swing Club is now is session." So Columbia decided to put this on the stage at Loew's State. And while we were playing there that week, an article came out in the New Yorker. And it was about -- the New Yorker had interviewed some woman -- I don't remember her name -- from Great Britain who played the (inaudible). And they had a profile on her. And at the end of her interview, they asked her what she wanted to do while she was in the United States. And she said she wanted to hear "Annie Laurie" and Loch Lomond whom she had heard God knows where.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

Well up until that time, Joe Helbock who was the owner of -- the operator of the Onyx Club -- he didn't think too much of what was happening. He was still trying to get Stuff Smith from the west coast.
But anyway, after he saw this article in the New Yorker, then they blew up by picture, put it out front, and called the New Yorker and said, 'You don't have to worry, here she is.'
